page0.text:
And...
After breakfast, I lay out my plans for the day.

page1.text:
"You're going to school?"
"Yes. Do you have a problem with that, Archer?"
"It's not a problem, but..."

page2.text:
Archer looks reluctant, but doesn't protest.
After spending a whole day with me, he probably understands now that Rin Tohsaka doesn't go back on her word once she's made up her mind.
I can sense his disagreement even if he doesn't voice it, but I've also learned that Archer has a sincere side beneath all the sarcasm. He won't whine about a decision he's accepted.

page3.text:
Yup, he's loyal—and awkward—like that.
That's what my intuition says, at least, after watching him yesterday.

page4.text: "Rin, now that you're a Master, you need to always be wary of enemy Masters. If you're ambushed at school, it'll be difficult to protect you."

page5.text: "Not necessarily. Listen here, Archer: I don't intend to alter my lifestyle just because of this. Besides, Masters fight out of public view, don't they? I don't think anyone would try to sneak up on me in front of everyone at school."

page6.text:
"...If that's your choice, then I'll follow along.
But at least let me stand guard in spirit form. Surely you don't intend to go there without me."

page7.text:
"Of course not. You'll stay with me whenever I'm outside, not just at school. That's a Servant's job, so I'm counting on you."
"I'm glad to hear it. A knight has a duty to repay his lord's trust. You won't be disappointed."

page8.text:
"Still, hypothetically speaking...what would you do if the enemy was in a place you thought safe?"
"Are we supposing that there's a Master at the school?"
"Yes. While it's hard for anyone who isn't a student or teacher to enter, it could spell trouble if a Master has already infiltrated."

page9.text: "I don't think that's likely. The Tohsaka are the only functioning mage family left in this town. The other one's gone belly up, so they won't produce any Masters."

page10.text:
"How do you know?"
"Hey, if there's any other mage families in Fuyuki besides the Tohsaka, you can bet I've looked into them already!
He isn't a Master; as the heir to that family, he can't wield the strength to become one. We can safely ignore them."

page11.text: "I see. So there is another mage at your school, but they lack the magical energy to be a Master."

page12.text:
"That's right. Most of the other Masters will be coming from the outside. They wouldn't be at my school."
"...For now, perhaps.
But there are exceptions to every rule, Rin. What will you do if you encounter an unknown mage at school?"

page13.text:
"I'm telling you, it won't happen. Mages are sensitive to each other. I've spent a whole year at that campus, so I'd be able to sense any mage no matter how hard they try to hide.
I'm certain that there are only two mages at school. Me, and that probie without enough power to be a Master.
Get it now? You're just being paranoid. The scenario you're imagining won't happen."

page14.text:
"Thus why I said hypothetical. But the unexpected has a way of happening.
Sometimes, destiny decides to make the impossible come about.
If we find ourselves in such a situation, I hope you'll remember not to take it out on me."

page15.text:
Archer chuckles dryly.
...His smug attitude already makes me want to do exactly that, but I'll be late for school if I let him keep pushing my buttons.

page16.text: "Look, it won't happen. It's a 'what-if' because it would never happen in the first place. And if it does, it would just mean that I was too naive."

page17.text:
"I'll remember you said that. Let's get going, then."
"It takes thirty minutes to get to your school, so you'd better leave soon if you want to be on time."

page18.text:
"I am legitimately shocked. It really did happen."
"I'm surprised as well. Ah, it really does pay to be a pessimist."

page19.text:
This is our exchange the moment we pass through the front gate.
It's almost time for homeroom, so there are students on their way to class
all around us.
Archer and I stand still like a pillar amid the swirling human sea.

page20.text:
"The air isn't just stagnant. Someone's set up a Bounded Field, don't you think?"
"It isn't finished, but yes, prep work is already underway.
They must think they're a big shot to go about it this openly..."

page21.text:
"More an unbelievable amateur. Only a third-rate mage would make such a conspicuous field. Someone with actual skills would conceal it until it was time to strike."
"And how would you rate this mage?"

page22.text:
"Who knows? I couldn't care less.
More importantly, trying such shoddy work in my territory is just gonna earn them a beating."

page23.text:
I let out an indignant huff as I cross through the grounds.
As a mage, there's no sugarcoating it. I won't be satisfied until whoever made this Bounded Field gets what's coming to them.

page24.text:
I'm on my way back from the music room after second period.
I spot a first-year floundering in the hallway.
She looks like she could use a hand with the large stack of documents she's carrying.

page25.text:
"Let me help, Sakura."
"Huh?"
"Ah. Tohsaka..."
"Printouts? Our class is supposed to take care of World History. What is that Kuzuki thinking, making you carry all these? Here, I'll take half."

page26.text:
"Ah... Thank you."
"It's fine. Are we taking these to your classroom?"
"...No, to Mr. Kuzuki. He said he needs to take them back because there's a typo."

page27.text:
"...I can believe that. Kuzuki's got such a huge stick up his butt, he once suspended an entire exam over a single typo."
"Hmm? You mean an exam here at this school?"

page28.text: "Yeah, it was during midterms last year. It was near the end when everyone's answer sheets were already filled. He just came out and said there's a typo, the questions are incorrect, the exam is suspended, and we'll redo it tomorrow. The teachers were as surprised as we were, and people still talk about it."

page29.text:
"That does sound like Mr. Kuzuki. He's the type of person who believes teachers shouldn't make any mistakes."
"But he goes overboard. You'd better learn while you can that once Kuzuki's got his mind set on something, he's as hard to move as a mountain."

page30.text:
"Hehe. You must like him. It's unusual to hear you talk about someone like that."
"Is it? I do wish he'd just relax..."
...Though he's all right just the way he is, ultimately.

page31.text:
The faculty at our school is made up of both really nice teachers and some real scary ones.
It's a delicate balance that Mr. Kuzuki's an important part of. He's the stick to the carrot.

page32.text:
"You'll see more of him next year, since he teaches Ethics.
...Oh right, Sakura. There's something I wanted to ask you."
"What is it?"
"It's about yesterday. Were you talking to a foreigner?"

page33.text:
"Ah... Y-you saw that?"
"I just happened to. What's going on? Is he someone you know?"
"...No. I, um, don't really know who he was. It sounded like he was lost. He asked a lot of questions, but I couldn't really understand what he was saying..."
Ah, and that's when she slipped away.

page34.text:
"I see. Sorry, I was just curious."
"No, I don't mind. Oh, it's just in here. I can get the rest, now."
"Okay. See you later, then."
I return the printouts to Sakura.
But before I head back to my classroom, I find myself stopping.

page35.text:
"How are you lately, Sakura?"
"Ah... I'm okay. I'm doing well."
"...I see. Let me know if Shinji's up to something. He doesn't know when to quit, so it'll just get worse if you keep quiet."

page36.text:
"You don't have to worry. He's been nice lately."
There isn't much I can say to a smile like that.
We say our farewells again, and I leave my underclassman acquaintance.

page37.text:
The school day is over.
The classrooms steadily empty, and the campus darkens by the hour.
The crimson sun will set soon.
Once night falls, there won't be anyone left around.

page38.text:
"Let's begin, Archer. First we'll investigate the Bounded Field. Once we determine what type it is, we'll decide whether to erase it or leave it."
I speak to my invisible partner.
I feel him nod in acknowledgement.

page39.text:
Bounded Fields are meant to protect their casters.
You can consider them a terrain-based magecraft formed by weaving magical energy into a net and applying it to the earth to affect the inside of the field.

page40.text:
There are countless types of effects they can have...
...ranging from wards that isolate an area from the outside world to avoid detection, to fields that limit the type of magecraft that can be activated within.
The most offensive type suppresses biological functions inside the area of effect,

page41.text:
and that's what's been applied to the school grounds.
While it isn't finished, everyone in the school will collapse once it's activated.

page42.text:
Something like that wouldn't work on me, though.
Bounded Fields are, after all, targeted at the area I'm in, not me specifically.
Such indirect magical interference won't affect a mage with magical energy flowing through her body.
Similarly, the electrical charges that flow in the atmosphere won't disturb the electrical currents within my body.

page43.text:
That means the Bounded Field has some other purpose.
Whoever it is that put this thing here isn't trying to defeat a Master with it.
I don't want to believe it, but they're targeting all the people within the school.
...There's only one possible reason for that.
It's a thought I can't stomach.

page44.text:
After checking all around campus, I finish my search on the roof.
It's thoroughly dark outside now.
The school gates shut at 6:00 PM, and it's now 8:00 PM.
Archer and I are the only ones left, and Archer's in his spirit form.

page45.text:
"...That makes the seventh one. Looks like this is the origin point."
There are eight symbols boldly drawn on the rooftop.
They're purplish-red marks that only a mage can see. I've never seen or heard of sigils like these.

page46.text:
"...Well, they've got me there. I don't know what to do about this."
Whoever set up this Bounded Field did it recklessly.
But while imprudent, the magical working itself is an order of magnitude beyond my own skills.
I could temporarily erase the energy of the curse, but I have no way to dispel the Bounded Field itself.
All the spellcaster needs to do is supply it with more energy to reactivate the curse's effects.

page47.text:
...
Archer doesn't comment.
...He's probably remained silent since encountering the rooftop sigils because he too has realized their nature.
This Bounded Field does more than drain its victims' stamina.
It will literally melt everyone inside once it's turned on.

page48.text:
There are Bounded Fields which rob victims of their life force and spiritual energy,
but the spell that's been applied to the school grounds is on a whole different level.
This is no less than a soul eater—a Blood Fort which melts the human bodies inside it and forcibly collects the souls that ooze out.

page49.text:
Since antiquity, souls have always been difficult to handle.
They're theorized to exist and are considered to be necessary components of magecraft, but only one mage has ever proven their existence.

page50.text:
Our definition of souls stops at "that which examines within" and "that which is transferred between vessels."
To not only extract souls but then capture them in one place? It defies comprehension.
What's a mage supposed to do with a bunch of energy we can't even convert?
So if I had to think of a purpose for it...

page51.text:
"Archer. Is that what you and your kind are?"
It comes out colder than I intended.

page52.text:
"...You surmise correctly. I did say that we are fundamentally spiritual beings. That means we feed on the Second and Third Factors: the soul and the mind.
Just as you sustain yourselves with the flesh of creatures, we Servants derive nutrition from the mind and soul.
While said nutrition doesn't change our base abilities, acquiring more of it does make us more durable. It increases our reserve of magical energy, in other words."

page53.text:
...He's right.
The way to make your own Servant stronger is to indiscriminately attack human beings.

page54.text:
"So your own Master's magical energy isn't enough?"
"It's sufficient, but it never hurts to have more. In war, some weaknesses can be compensated with material when one is lacking in fighting strength.
It's a basic strategy for a Master to take energy from the humans around them. In that sense, this Bounded Field is an efficient tactic."

page55.text:
...
Archer's saying that I should murder people and take their power if I want to win.
It's so simple.
I've always known this to be true,
and I know it's the path I'm supposed to walk.

page56.text:
"That really tees me off. Don't ever bring it up again, Archer."
Staring at the sigils, I make my stance clear.
Oddly, Archer sounds just as put off.
"I agree. I'd never do such a thing."
His answer comes firm and resolute.

page57.text:
"...Time to erase this, then. It won't do much good, but I can at least slow it down."
I approach the sigil and extend my left hand.
The Magic Crest engraved on my arm is like a grimoire passed down through the Tohsaka line.

page58.text:
A mental switch is flicked.
I pass magical energy through the Magic Crest, load a verse of Bounded Field erasure, take a deep breath, and activate it.

page59.text:
"Abzug. (Erase.) Bedienung. (Surgical removal.) Mittelstand. (Verse two.)"
I then send a pulse of magical energy via my left hand.
That should wash away the sigil for now—
"What, you're gonna erase it? What a waste."
Suddenly,
a third voice chimes in while I'm casting the spell.

page60.text:
"...!"
I whirl around.
A man is perched on top of the water tower,
some ten meters above, looking down at me.

page61.text:
He's clad in a deep blue that blends into the night.
His mouth is drawn into a grin, and he has a bestial air about him.
...The beast's gaze is sharp and clear.
In this bizarre situation, the man in blue watches me as if he's greeting a friend he hasn't seen in a decade.

page63.text: "Nah. It's a mage's job to play little tricks. We just fight whomever we're ordered to. Isn't that right, mate?"

page64.text:
"...!"
His tone is lethal yet carefree.
This man can see Archer!

page65.text:
"You're a Servant!"
"That I am. And if you know that, lass, you must be my enemy."
"..."
My spine tenses.
The man's voice is detached and nonchalant.
But it's colder than anyone I've ever heard—so scary it's nauseating.

page66.text:
...
What's the best move here? I don't know.
But my brain is still working enough to tell me that I absolutely must not fight him...!

page67.text:
"...Oh? I'm impressed. Here I was thinking you don't know heads from tails, but you figured out what really counts.
Ugh, I blew that. Shouldn't have gone outta my way to taunt you."
The man raises an arm.
...
It appears in a flash.
His once empty hand now holds
a scarlet, two meter-long weapon.

page68.text:
"Hah...!"
My legs throw me to the side before I can think.
There isn't time to even hesitate about jumping off the roof.
With all my might, I make a mad dash for the fence, intending to barrel right through it!

page69.text:
A cyclone lifts my hair into the air.
It was by the skin of my teeth—
In that instant, something slices through the space I was just in, tearing the fence apart with it.

page70.text:
"Ha. You've got a nice pair of legs on you!"
A blue whirlwind pursues me.
There's no way out.
The fence is behind me. My flanks are cut off. I won't make it...!

page71.text:
"Es ist gros (Light mass), Es ist klein (heavy pressure)...!"
I react swiftly.
My Magic Crest surges to life so I can weave a single-count magecraft.
The spell lightens mass and manipulates gravity.
Light as a feather, my body bounds into the air...

page72.text:
"Rin!"
"I know! I got this!"
...and I jump over the fence to plummet off the roof.

page73.text:
"...!"
Air resistance and gravity push and pull along my body.
It's about 15 meters to the ground, 1.7 seconds away—too slow, he's going to catch up to me!

page74.text:
"Vox Gott (Cite precept), Es Atlas (the funeral returns to the earth)!
Archer, handle the landing!"

page75.text:
"...Hah!"
I let Archer absorb the shock of the landing, and break into a dash as soon as we touch down.
I couldn't stay on that rooftop.
We need a less cramped arena from which to maneuver freely.
A battlefield without obstacles, where Archer and I can truly shine...!

page76.text:
"Hah, hah...!"
It takes me less than seven seconds to escape from the roof to the schoolyard.
A distance of over a hundred meters, crossed at a pace no normal person can manage, much less clearly see.

page77.text:
And yet...
"You really do have good legs. I almost feel bad about having to kill you here."
Against a Servant, it's wasted effort.

page78.text:
"Archer!"
At the same time I draw back, Archer materializes before me.
It's a cloudy night.
Archer's hand grips a shortsword that faintly reflects the moonlight.

page79.text:
"...Oh?"
The man's lips twist into an ominous sneer.
"...Yeah, that's how this oughta be. Can't say I hate guys like you who are quick on the uptake."
The whirlwind howls.
It's the weapon he swung at me on the rooftop: a spear of blood-like crimson that came mercilessly for my head.

page80.text:
"A Lancer..."
"That's me. That must make your Servant a Saber...
nah, he doesn't feel like one. Who the hell are you?"
Gone is his carefree ease from a moment ago.
Archer stays silent, facing off against Lancer's unconcealed bloodlust.

page81.text:
...There's just under five meters between them.
Lancer's weapon is nearly two meters long.
It doesn't feel like this beast of a man is going to be deterred by a mere three meter difference.

page82.text:
"...Hmph. I can tell you're not the type to settle things man-to-man. That must make you Archer."
Archer doesn't take the bait.
An unusual clash of blue and red stare each other down.
The two knights, somewhat similarly dressed, mutually calculate the other's demise.

page83.text:
"...All right. All that's left is to throw down. Draw your bow, Archer.
Not how I usually do this, but I'm polite enough to wait that long."
...
Archer doesn't answer.
His back, as steely as a sword, seems to convey that
he must not have anything to say to someone he must defeat.

page84.text:
...
That's when I realize it.
...I'm such a fool. Archer was waiting for my word.

page85.text:
"Archer."
I call out to him without getting any closer.
"Don't hold back. Show me everything you've got."
"...Heh."
Was that a laugh?
The red knight surges forward, his lips curled in response.

page86.text:
Wind swirls.
A scarlet bullet flies forth, blade in hand.
"Fool!"
A blue spear thrust intercepts him.
If the charging Archer is a gust of wind, then the speartip that rises to meet him is a divine storm.

page87.text:
Streaking blades. Elegant parries.
Archer is put on the defensive, fending off the swift thrusts with his short sword.

page88.text:
"Rgh!"
The man in red is stopped in his tracks,
his advance denied by the enemy.
He can't even breach the two-meter coverage of the spear.
A polearm wielder can control his opponent's range.
Lancer, with his nearly two-meter reach, needs to simply engage his foe whenever he comes within range.
It's easier for him to stab an advancing opponent than it is for him to go after Archer himself.

page89.text:
Despite this...
Lancer closes the distance himself to press the attack, all the while keeping Archer from advancing further.

page90.text:
"You're a damn fool of a bowman, trying to challenge me in close combat!"
Lancer's snarl is fiery.
With each thrust, Lancer closes in, the assault never letting up for a second.

page91.text:
...Moving in too close is suicide for a spear wielder.
The advantage of a spear is the ability to control the enemy's position.
Lancer shouldn't have a chance if he keeps closing in.

page92.text:
"No way."
But that's only according to conventional wisdom.
Unerringly, unceasingly, Lancer's spear seeks to pierce Archer's throat, shoulder, forehead, heart.

page93.text:
The strikes are too swift to even leave an after-image.
Archer is forced to parry, block, or evade every move of the spear. Any strike, if true, would be a mortal blow.
Still, Archer is a Servant, even if he specializes with the bow.
He won't be brought down so easily by mundane attacks!

page94.text:
"Hngh!"
The thrust at his forehead is quickly batted aside, and Archer renews his charge in spite of Lancer's spear.

page95.text:
One might think that swordplay is all there is to Archer's attacks, but he's exploiting a weakness of spear tactics.
Against a spear's considerable reach, neither retreat nor evasion are viable defenses for long.

page96.text:
A half-hearted withdrawal isn't enough to get out of range, while probing attacks will lead to evisceration.
A reckless charge will similarly end in impalement at the edge of the spear's range.
Archer and Lancer have more or less the same physical stature.
Without heavy armor, it's difficult for Archer to penetrate the lethal storm of Lancer's attack radius.

page97.text:
But Lancer's strikes are a different story.
The high-speed thrusts, intended to pierce vital points, are indeed terrifying.
But each strike has a set trajectory and target; if one can predict these, then there are ways to avoid harm.
Just as Archer is doing, one can block the strikes aimed at vital points or just barely evade their arcs to create safe openings.

page98.text:
Lancer probably underestimated him as a ranged specialist.
The advantage of a long weapon is the generous range at which one can engage the opponent. By giving that up, Lancer has assured his—

page99.text:
...
"Ngh!?"
The man in red stops in his tracks.
I watch a nightmare unfold, as if time has rewinded.
Lancer's attacks become even faster than before.

page100.text:
"Guh...!"
Archer's short sword is knocked aside, as he twists to avoid being skewered.
Lancer's spear doesn't allow retreat.
Or rather, his endless attacks are so fierce and sharp that even Servants are doomed against them!

page101.text:
...
We were the ones who underestimated our enemy.
That Servant, that Lancer and his spear can't be described in mundane martial terms.

page102.text:
Who could possibly survive such a relentless barrage?
Archer beats a desperate retreat while parrying strikes, creating slightly more distance between the fighters.
In that moment...
Lancer steps into the gap and unleashes an even more ferocious attack.

page103.text:
The storm of attacks is little different from what he's already been doing,
but their execution is truly godlike.
They've already clashed ten times.
No. It's actually several times more than that.
The torrent of spear strikes increases again in intensity and number, threatening to take Archer's life a thousand times over.

page104.text:
It isn't even a change in speed, but in precision.
At a steady pace, Lancer's spear comes down on Archer like a waterfall.
How can Archer get inside his guard?
With such a short weapon, all he can do is defend against the spear.
He has no way to close in on Lancer. In fact, he's being forced backwards.

page105.text:
"..."
The steel vacuum stretches out.
I...I should be backing Archer up, but the right words die in my throat.
My magecraft isn't easy to aim precisely.
I risk hitting Archer too if he can't get far away enough from Lancer.
Meanwhile, Lancer's advantage will only deepen.

page106.text:
And, to be honest...
I'm captivated by their duel.
So this is a battle between Servants.
The Holy Grail War is a battle between familiars of the highest order: Heroic Spirits, beings that we mages can't begin to approach.

page107.text:
Servants.
Familiars divided among seven classes and roles, serving seven Masters.
Supreme familiars called forth by the Holy Grail itself.

page108.text:
"Familiar" is really a misnomer for them.
Familiars are supposed to be subservient minions who act on behalf of a mage.
Normally, you'd imagine something like Puss in Boots,
an elegant white bird,
or a disobedient black dog. Something like that.

page109.text:
Those sorts of familiars are what a typical mage can manage to command.
Familiars are just that. From the Latin for a menial servant.
It's inconceivable that a mascot used for menial labor would be stronger than its master.
Servants are a different story.
They're quite literally the most powerful examples of humanity.
Even the five Magicians wouldn't be able to control them.

page110.text:
It's difficult to summon a Servant, but not because Servants are more powerful than mages.
Servants are beings that surpass magecraft itself.

page111.text:
To be clear...
Servants are heroes of the past.
Myths. Legends. Fables. Histories.
We call the glorious superhumans from our traditions "heroes," whether the tales are true or not.

page112.text:
Immortalized by what humanity says about them, they cease to be merely human after death, and ascend to something greater.
...People who work miracles, who save the multitudes, who accomplish great feats, are elevated to the status of heroes, either in life or after death.
They become a type of Elemental we call Heroic Spirits—guardians of the human race.

page113.text:
It doesn't matter whether they were historical people or characters from mythology.
Heroes are created by the thoughts of the people.
We imagine them as the idols we wish they were and treat them as if they were real.
Objective truth is irrelevant.
Fame and faith are sufficient to give form to these legends.

page114.text:
They're humanity's ultimate ideals, the greatest among us.
That's what it means to be hero and a Heroic Spirit.
Naturally, it's impossible for a mere human to control something greater than human.
What mages usually do is borrow a portion of their power and imitate their feats.
Summoning a complete Heroic Spirit is simply impossible.

page115.text:
Yet the Holy Grail makes it possible.
It allows us to summon these spirits in the flesh and even bind them to our command.
The sheer absurdity of it proves the Grail's omnipotence.

page116.text:
That's how Heroic Spirits are summoned from across time, whether from the Age of Gods or as recent as a century ago.
The seven Heroic Spirits serve and protect their seven Masters, and each Master sends their Servants out to defeat enemy Masters.
...It's a deathmatch between heroes of every age and every land.
That's the story behind the ritual we call the Holy Grail War.

page117.text:
...Of course, there are limits to what the Grail can do.
Even the Holy Grail can't indiscriminately summon mythic beings akin to Elementals.
Just as a form created by the people is required to materialize the Sixth Theoretical Factor known as Demons,
Heroic Spirits need a material form to operate in this world.

page118.text:
This is their temporary label, and the way they're allowed to exist in this world.
The Holy Grail provides vessels that Heroic Spirits can easily materialize in, called "classes," and only Heroic Spirits that fit these classes can be summoned.
A class is like a passport that lets a Heroic Spirit visit the modern era to act as a familiar. It's a material vessel that they temporarily possess.

page119.text: There are seven Masters, and seven Heroic Spirits to serve them.

page120.text:
Each is assigned one of seven classes:
Saber, the knight of the sword.
Lancer, the knight of the spear.
Archer, the knight of the bow.
Rider, the cavalier.
Caster, the mage.
Assassin, the silent killer.
Berserker, the mad warrior.
Only Heroic Spirits with attributes corresponding to the seven classes can be summoned to the modern world, and they become Servants whom the Masters command.

page121.text:
That's the Servant system.
Humans summon and make contracts with Heroic Spirits beyond our ability to handle, all in hopes of winning a miracle beyond our ken.
It's the greatest of battles that can only happen here in this land, like no other Holy Grail War!

page122.text:
"...!"
The duel reaches an even higher pitch.
The short sword goes flying from Archer's hand after blocking one of Lancer's strikes.
Lancer's skill is consummate.
A seemingly straight thrust suddenly whipped into a disarming arc at Archer's wrist.
It was an attack that Archer couldn't have avoided, even if he saw it coming.

page123.text:
There isn't an effective way to parry the spear with his sword.
A forceful block is countered with an even keener strike, while defending with minimal force will never create an opening to exploit.
The clash between sword and spear is shaping up into an intense struggle to defeat an enemy outside of Archer's reach...

page124.text:
"You fool."
There's no hesitation in Lancer, even as he taunts Archer.
He pauses from the constant pressure he puts on Archer.
Does he intend to settle the duel in an instant?
Lancer takes a firmly rooted stance, trading a fiery glare
with the now unarmed Archer.

page125.text:
It happens in an instant.
In the span of a breath, Lancer looses a flurry of blows that's no less than a flash of light.
Imperceptible.
Forehead, neck, and heart.
The spear moves to skewer all three!

page126.text:
And yet...
Another flash of light counters the first that I couldn't even follow!

page127.text:
"...!?"
Archer's hand grasps a shortsword once more.
Like the weapon he used earlier, it's a Chinese sword not dissimilar to a cleaver.
But the greatest difference between them is...
"Tch! A dual-wielder, eh!?"
Blade and blade.
In each hand he grips a sword, each clearly meant to complement the other.

page128.text:
"Ha! Playing swordsman, are we!?"
Lancer's spear sings through the air.
It becomes even faster, as if to herald Archer's certain death.

page130.text:
The duel becomes a symphony of clashing blades.
Two steel instruments play a resounding chorus,
the sparks of their conflict rising to a never-ending crescendo.

page131.text:
Their battle is like a vacuum.
It sucks in all the air around it, making me feel like I'll be cut if I even dare to approach.
...
It all happened in an instant, really.
But as I watched with bated breath, the moment seemed to stretch on.

page132.text:
Lancer keeps his foe out of his fatal pocket,
while Archer attempts to close the gap with his shield of dual swords.
They've clashed over a hundred times already, Archer losing a weapon each time.

page133.text:
But instantly, another sword appears in Archer's empty hand, and Lancer is slightly driven back each time.
Lancer finally acknowledges his miscalculation.
He has no idea who he's fighting.
But it would be a mistake to keep dismissing his opponent as a bowman.

page134.text:
A space opens up between them.
Lancer puts significant distance between them. Maybe he intends to start over.
...That agility isn't normal.
Archer's charge defies human ability, but he's sluggish next to Lancer.
The swiftness of Lancer's retreat had the speed and grace of a leopard.

page135.text:
"...Twenty-seven. I've disarmed you twenty-seven times, and you still have more?"
Lancer sounds irritated.
Actually, he sounds more confused than upset.

page136.text:
...I feel the same way.
According to my father, Servants typically only have one weapon.
They're supposed to be singular relics of unimaginable power, not expendable items to be drawn over and over like Archer's doing.

page137.text:
Servants are heroes whose spiritual rank are elevated to the magnitude of Elementals or Divine Spirits after death.
In a way, they're not unlike angels and demons.
They're powerful familiars on their own, but their greatest strength is the mighty weapons that prove they're heroes. We call these magic items Noble Phantasms.

page138.text:
They are the favored weapon or armor that a Servant used while it was a living hero, and it's literally the Servant's secret weapon.
To a Servant, a Noble Phantasm is a one-of-a-kind armament.
It's the Servant's indispensible ultimate weapon as well.

page139.text:
The same goes for Lancer's spear, it can exhibit its power as a Noble Phantasm if he so chooses.
A Noble Phantasm is a formidable weapon on its own, but its true power is expressed by invoking its True Name.

page140.text:
Heroes' weapons are known to have slain dragons and gods; to have conquered the earth.
Servants activate Noble Phantams with their own magical energy.
It's not unlike magecraft, actually.
Servants use their Noble Phantasms as catalysts to recreate the destruction from their legends.

page141.text:
A Noble Phantasm is most certainly not a disposable tool.
Archer has produced dozens of swords by now. Each seems like a masterwork unto itself, but they surely can't be his Noble Phantasm.
He's an Archer, after all.
His secret weapon must be some kind of bow.

page142.text:
"What's the matter, Lancer? It's not like you to be so cautious. Where did all that fire go?"
"Tch, sneaky bastard. Think you can bait me like that?"

page143.text:
The cause of Lancer's irritation is obvious.
Lancer has been fighting as a spearman, while Archer has been fending him off as a swordsman.
Meaning that Archer hasn't revealed his cards yet.
That must be frustrating to deal with.

page144.text:
"Fine, then let me ask you this: which land are you a hero from?
I've never heard of a bowman who's also a dual-wielding swordsman."
"It's easy to tell who you are, though. They say that only the swiftest heroes are chosen as Lancers, but you're outstanding even among them.
There can't be three spear-wielders as fine as you in the world. And only one has such bestial agility."

page145.text:
"Oh? Well said, Archer."
For a moment,
the bloodlust is so strong, I forget to breathe.

page146.text:
Lancer's arms move.
It's a deliberate stance, without any of the nonchalance he's shown thus far.
His speartip dips, as if to puncture the ground. But Lancer's eyes bore straight through Archer.
"Then will you taste my killer technique?"
"I won't stop you. You're a foe we have to overcome sooner or later."

page147.text:
Lancer lowers his stance.
Simultaneously,
a thorny, bitter cold overtakes the schoolyard.

page148.text:
...The air freezes.
I don't mean that metaphorically; it's literally ice-cold.
All of the mana in the atmosphere freezes solid.
Only the warrior Lancer is allowed to breathe in this space.
The spear in Lancer's hands is undoubtedly magical.
It's true form eager to burst forth.

page149.text:
Oh, no.
He's going to die.
I don't know what kind of Noble Phantasm that is, but Archer is finished.
It's the first time I've had this kind of premonition, and hard as it is to believe, I don't doubt it for a second.

page150.text:
If Lancer unleashes his spear, Archer will die.
That's absolutely certain.
As Lancer says, his spear means death.

page151.text:
"...Ah."
Archer will lose.
Lancer will stab him through the heart, and he'll die.

page152.text:
Despite that...
Despite these premonitions, despite this insight, I can't even help Archer.
I feel like if I so much as lift a finger, it'll signal the beginning of the end.

page153.text:
If there's a way to prevent Archer's defeat, then it can only be...
"WHO GOES THERE!?"
...the sudden appearance of a third party whom we've all overlooked.

page154.text:
"Huh?"
Lancer's ferocity disappears.
I hear the sound of someone running away.
...From behind, I can clearly make out a school uniform.

page155.text:
"A student!? Someone was still on campus!?"
"Apparently. And it saved our lives."
Archer answers coolly.
Sure enough, the interruption did save our skin.

page156.text:
"...I screwed up. I was so distracted by Lancer that I wasn't keeping an eye on our surroundings. Wait, what are you doing, Archer?"
"Can't you tell? I'm resting because there's no one left to fight."
"That's not what I mean! What about Lancer?"
"He went off to chase the witness. Probably to get rid of them."
...
For a moment,
my thoughts grind to a halt.

page157.text:
"After them, Archer! I'll catch up!"
...
Archer pursues Lancer immediately.

page158.text:
"Damn it! I'm such a dummy!"
I curse my own negligence.
It's standard mage policy to eliminate witnesses.
...Until now, I've been careful not to allow anyone to see me as a mage to avoid that scenario. Why did it have to happen today, of all days!?

page159.text:
The night feels oppressive, not letting even the moonlight through.
I find Archer standing over the body of a student, collapsed on the floor of a terribly cold hallway.

page160.text:
"..."
He looks wordlessly down at the student.
...An odor reaches my nose.
The sight of slowly pooling blood makes me realize that it's the smell of death.

page161.text:
"...Follow him, Archer. Lancer should be running back to his Master. If we can at least catch sight of their face, then tonight isn't a total loss."
...
Archer goes off after Lancer.
Only the fallen student and I remain in the corridor.

page162.text:
"..."
I can't look him in the eye.
But I have to.
This is my fault.
This is my fault.
This is my fault.

page163.text:
Since I was young...
Since I made up my mind to inherit the Tohsaka legacy, I've been prepared for this.
Mages aren't governed by good or evil.
I've known all along that this path would be a bloody one...!

page164.text:
"A single thrust from Lancer's spear. If he got you in the heart, there's no saving you."
I don't know how many seconds ago Lancer killed him.
It's just a matter of whether he was unlucky enough to get stabbed through the heart.
The blood loss isn't as bad as I would expect for a destroyed heart, so maybe the injury isn't too deep.

page165.text:
It might not be too bad, but he's still screwed if blood has been cut off to his brain.
Though, yeah, if his heart was wrecked, then he would've died instantly.

page166.text:
"...Still not dead? You're really something."
It's hard to hear, but just barely...
My ears pick up faint breathing that might be a death rattle.
But it won't last more than a few seconds.
I don't have the power to save him. I don't even have a way to heal my own wounds.

page167.text:
"I have to look him in the eye, at least."
I start to reach for the face of the prone figure, when I realize that my fingers won't move.
...They're shaking.
But...why?
I'm used to this.
I've made this choice countless times.

page168.text:
I've lost so much thanks to my own mistakes, my own selfishness.
That's why I've always been ready for this day to come.
Then...why am I so angry at myself?

page169.text:
"...I'm sorry. I'll keep you company. You deserve that much."
I use cold logic to still my trembling fingers and legs, and check the fallen student's face.
...
A great weight falls onto me.
I feel like I've just been struck by a hammer.

page170.text:
"...Don't do this to me. Why did it have to be you?"
I grind my teeth.
No longer to brace myself against the shaking,
but because I'm truly angry.
Why did it have to be him?
Why him especially?
I'm not upset with Lancer for silencing a witness, as a Servant should.
But at school today of all days, at this hour!? You fool, why would you of all people...!?

page171.text:
...
Sakura's face comes to mind.
I'm sure she'll cry.
And I find myself recalling a day after school, some years ago.
...The sky glowed a distant red.
A boy that always ran.
And a silly little girl watched him absently from afar.
...That boy got involved in something he shouldn't have, and now his corpse is front of me.

page172.text:
...
...There's still a way.
If I fail, I might lose my trump card, but there's a way to save him.
Ugh, no. I'll lose it whether this works or not, so the outcome is the same to me.

page173.text:
...
This is a mistake.
His impending death is a foregone conclusion.
It's my fault for not paying enough attention to what was happening around me,
and his fault for having the dumb luck to be here tonight.

page174.text:
There's no need for me to go this far for him.
My father, who left me with nothing to remember him by, did in fact leave me this heirloom to help me.
It's a massive store of magical energy meant to be a trump card that helps me win this war.
A precious, precious treasure, just for...

page175.text:
"...So what, stupid?"
I turn back and kneel by the dying boy.

page176.text:
"...Well, that's that."
The pendant in my hand gets lighter.
My father's keepsake is nearly empty.
With a clink, I drop it on the guy who was a second away from becoming a corpse.

page177.text:
"...Nothing else I could've done."
There really was no other way.
I don't have the power or skill to bring someone back to life. Especially not someone with a destroyed heart, damaged blood vessels, and brain death mere seconds away.
All I can do is patch up his missing parts with brute force.

page178.text:
"You're lucky to still be breathing. If you were totally dead, then there would've been no bringing you back with any amount of magical energy."
But if he's still alive...
Then I just need to help him the best I can.

page179.text:
"...I would've really hated myself if I failed, but it worked out, I guess... Yeah, I feel fulfilled, if I'm being honest. This wasn't such a bad experience."
Though really, I'm lying to myself.

page180.text:
"...I should go. I did what I came to do. Better get out of here before he wakes up."
Yeah, there isn't any point hanging around.
Archer's off tailing Lancer, so I should just go home.

page181.text:
...On the way home, I remember.
I left my father's memento at school. Though now it's just a pendant with all of its magical energy wrung dry.

page182.text:
"...Oh, well."
I don't suppose I need it anymore.
It might have a little bit of energy left in it, but it's less than the ten gemstones I'm carrying.
What Father wanted was for me to have enough magical energy to win the Holy Grail War.
Now that I've used that resource up, its container doesn't mean much.

page183.text:
I arrive home without announcing my return and plop down on the sofa.
Archer still isn't back yet.
I heave a tired sigh and listen to the clock tick for a few minutes.

page184.text:
"...Argh, I need to get my head in the game.
After a battle like that, what am I even spacing out for?"

page185.text:
I jump to my feet and make some black tea.
I have plenty to think about.
The Servant we encountered most of all.
I finally watched a battle between Servants, which, until today, I'd only known about through books.

page186.text: "Lancer, huh...I panicked when he seemed about to use his Noble Phantasm, but at least it would have let us learn who he is..."

page187.text:
Learning a Servant's identity is key to defeating a Servant.
With the exception of the idiot who doesn't know his own name, a Servant's greatest weakness is their identity.
Once you learn a Servant's name and identity, then you can mostly deduce that Heroic Spirit's Noble Phantasm.

page188.text:
It goes without saying that since Servants are Heroic Spirits, they have legends associated with them.
Unraveling their history can reveal a lot about their abilities.
Masters address Servants by their class names to hide their True Names.
The more famous a hero, the more likely their weapons and weaknesses are to be known.

page189.text:
A Heroic Spirit who has become a Servant will never willingly divulge their identity.
That knowledge is reserved only for their Master.
There's a tacit understanding that a Master conceals their own Servant's identity while trying to figure out the identities of the other Servants.

page190.text:
...Including this one, there have been five Holy Grail Wars thus far.
Each Servant's quality depends on the caliber of the summoned Heroic Spirit.
Naturally, a famous hero, or one with a legendary weapon, is powerful.

page191.text:
Accordingly, it's difficult to summon such Heroic Spirits.
For that, a summoner needs a connection to the Heroic Spirit they're summoning, such as a weapon the hero wielded during their lifetime.
Even the Mage's Association, with all its resources, only has a few such items in its possession.
That's why most mages, myself included, summon a Heroic Spirit whom we have an affinity with.

page192.text:
A Servant's strength is determined by the caliber of the Heroic Spirit, or so the logic goes.
But reality isn't so clear-cut. Even a superior Heroic Spirit might struggle when the classes in play aren't favorable.
Class-specific abilities can have a large impact on the outcome of a battle.

page193.text:
Each of the seven classes comes with additional abilities, and the interaction between these can allow one to triumph over a stronger opponent.
To continue the example, it's said that great heroes were defeated by lesser-known heroes in each of the previous four wars.
As far as I know, the best Servant class is Saber.

page194.text:
Saber fought until the very end in each of the last four wars.
Saber, Lancer, and Archer are said to have powerful Magic Resistance.
Magecraft isn't effective against these three classes.

page195.text:
After all, they're warriors from ages of myth and legend, when magic was still prevalent.
Spells cast by modern mages would probably fizzle out on contact.
...That's why the first three classes are generally considered the most desirable.

page196.text:
The other class to watch out for is Berserker.
Heroic Spirits summoned in this class lose their sanity.
As the name suggests, they become crazed warriors and puppets of their Masters, but are strengthened beyond the powers they had in life.

page197.text:
It's also worth noting that the stronger a Servant is, the greater its burden on its Master.
In the past, Masters who drew Berserkers couldn't control their Servants, and ultimately self-destructed due to running out of magical energy.
No exceptions.

page198.text:
...In the vast majority of cases, Holy Grail Wars are won by the summoned Servants' abilities.
Of course, there are plenty of ways for Masters to win battles, but it basically comes down to fighting between Servants.
That's why a Master needs to commit the utmost diligence and effort to summoning a Servant...

page199.text:
...
Discontented, I decide to come up with projections for the battles to come.
Before long, it's 11:00 PM... Yes, I fixed the clocks already. Archer comes home.

page200.text:
"Welcome back. How'd it go?"
"...Sorry, I failed. His Master must be a cautious one. I was at least able to tell that Lancer's Master isn't on this side of the city."

page201.text:
Figures.
Lancer was all alone, and his Master didn't seem like the type to show themselves.

page202.text:
"I see. Well, we knew it wouldn't be that easy."
Everything can't go according to plan.
So there's no use worrying over it.
I'll just give up and treat tonight as a learning experience.

page203.text: "You seem dispirited, Master. What happened to all that combativeness? Don't tell me you're cowed after a single skirmish. If you order it, I can go back out right now and reengage Lancer."

page204.text:
Archer doesn't say it, but I can tell he thinks that's the right course of action.
...Oh.
I must look pretty depressed right now, huh?

page205.text:
"That's not it at all. I'm not going back out there because I don't want to waste the effort."
"Hm? Waste what effort?"
"The Masters aren't all accounted for yet. Tonight's fight was unavoidable, but we're not supposed to fight until the signal to start the war. Father told me that's a rule of the Holy Grail War."

page206.text:
"...I see. So your father was a Master, too."
Archer nods in understanding.
Actually...
...he's making a rather mixed expression.

page207.text:
"What? You got something to say to me?"
"Yes, I forgot to ask you something.
Rin, you've been raised from a young age to be a Master and followed that lifestyle accordingly, yes? That means you always expected to become a Master."

page208.text: "Of course I did. Some mages are appointed as Masters, but it doesn't work like that for me. I'm a Tohsaka. Winning the Holy Grail War has been our goal for generations."

page209.text:
"That makes sense. So you already had an objective in mind.
That's what I wanted to ask you about. I need to know my Master's wish before I offer my sword in service.
So, Rin. What is your wish?"
"My wish? I don't really have one."
"...What?"
Aha, Archer's making a funny face.

page210.text:
"Th-that can't be true! The Holy Grail can grant any wish. Mages only become Masters to obtain the Holy Grail. So what do you mean, you have no wish!?"
...
Archer drops all pretense.

page211.text:
...Ah, right.
Once the Holy Grail is won, the victorious Master's wish has nothing to do with the Servant.
But that's weird. Father mentioned that Servants have their own wishes too, but that's their own business.
It shouldn't matter to Archer whether or not I have a wish.

page212.text:
"Fine. Since you don't have a specific wish, what about a general one? Like conquering the world, for example."
"Why? The world already belongs to me."

page213.text:
...
"You know, Archer, the 'world' is just the set of values that revolves around yourself. I've had that ever since I was born. I don't need to take over something that's always been inherently mine."

page214.text:
...
Archer looks at me with a strange expression.
Man, he's stubborn.

page215.text:
"I don't believe you. The Holy Grail has the power to grant wishes. You could obtain anything you want in the material world. How can you not desire anything at all?"
"World domination sounds like a pain, and I wouldn't know what to do with it. Not everyone looks at things the way you do, you know."
"...I'm having trouble understanding this. What do you fight for?"

page216.text:
"If there's a fight to be had, I just want in, Archer. I'll take whatever I find along the way. I don't really know how the Holy Grail works, but if I find that there's something I want, I can just use it on that. Not all people live to acquire things, you know."
"Meaning..."
"That's right. I'm just fighting to win."

page217.text:
...
Archer sighs and shrugs.
Maybe he's fed up with me, but he finally relaxes.

page218.text:
"...I give up. You truly are fit to be my Master."
...Uh.
I...don't know how to respond to comments like that, so I wish he'd stop making them...

page219.text:
"...Hmph. Servants may not have the right to choose their Masters, but what makes you think I'm worthy of you?"
"Do I need to spell it out? It's because you are, without a doubt, the strongest Master.
I don't need any other reason than that."
"Oh. Well, thanks. That doesn't sound like flattery, coming from you."
...I turn away to hide my embarrassment.

page220.text:
Archer usually acts like a smartass, so this sincerity is blindsiding me.
...Admittedly, I'm happy he feels this way.
I've come to trust him, and he's come to trust me.
I don't think this mutual sentiment is a bad thing.

page221.text:
"I suppose we should take a breather, then. The seventh Master has yet to appear, but it might not happen right—Wait, Rin. What happened to your jewelry?"
"My jewelry? Oh, you mean the pendant? ...I forgot it back there. It doesn't have any power anymore, so I don't really need it, do I?"

page222.text:
"I suppose not. If you say so."
"Yeah. It's a keepsake from Father, but it's hardly the only memory I have of him—"
"Don't say that. You don't always have to act so strong, Rin."
As he nags me,
Archer holds out the pendant I left at school.

page223.text:
"Oh. You picked it up for me."
"...Don't lose it again. It really belongs with you, Rin."
Archer avoids eye contact as he passes the pendant to me, looking almost bashful.

page224.text:
"...Okay. Thanks."
I accept it.
To be honest, I'm not sure whether to be embarrassed or play it off right now.

page225.text:
The pendant is as I left it.
...As I thought, it really doesn't have any energy left.
It's just an expensive jewel now that it's empty.
But to put it in Archer's terms...
Maybe it still has meaning as a memento of my father, even without its power.
I suppose I can laugh this off as a net win, since I spent my trump card to save someone's life.

page226.text:
"...Wait a second."
I jolt up in my seat.
I wasn't thinking straight while I lamented what I lost, but as I pull myself together, it strikes me.

page227.text:
He saw us, so I ought to alter his memories.
Meanwhile, Lancer prioritized eliminating witnesses over fighting us.
Lancer's thinking should reflect that of his Master.
Which means...if a Master who went out of their way to kill a witness finds out that he survived...

page228.text:
"They won't let him live."
I stand up from the sofa.
...It's already been three hours.
I might not make it in time,
but I can't let this happen, not after all the trouble I went through!

page229.text:
I sprint through the night.
Fortunately, I know where he lives.
Not because I bothered to find out, but because someone I happen to know goes over to his place often. I've never been there personally.

page230.text:
"...Good grief. You're really making this harder on yourself."
Archer gripes unenthusiastically.
It's going to be as much of a struggle to rescue the guy now as it was to save him earlier.

page231.text:
It's midnight. The sky is shrouded in clouds.
I arrive at an old samurai estate.

page232.text:
The building closest to the outside shows no signs of life.
There aren't many neighboring houses, so it's unlikely anyone would come even if they noticed something was amiss.

page233.text:
...
My breath mists white.
The wind picks up.
It must be pretty strong, because the clouds are starting to move.
I find myself trembling despite the temperate Fuyuki weather, and a chill runs down my spine.

page234.text: People call Fuyuki a warm place, but you can feel the winter chill from the hilltops.

page235.text:
The air is bitingly cold.
The chill presses in and makes it hard to hear.
In the midst of this air that seems conquered by the cold, I keenly sense the enemy.

page236.text:
"He's here. The Lancer from earlier!"
I bite my lip.
Something's on the other side of the outer wall.
Lancer must have already infiltrated the house, waiting for its witless owner to come home to his death.

page237.text:
"...We'll just have to jump over. I'll think about what happens when it happens!"
Just as I'm about to order Archer to go in...
A flash.
From the house emerges a radiant white light bright as the sun.

page238.text:
...
Its presence is all-consuming.
The power radiating from Lancer is being washed away by the newcomer's even greater aura.
...An instantaneous explosion of ether gives the spirit physical form,
and the summoned being overpowers Lancer.

page239.text:
"No way..."
All I can do is whisper in awe.
But the truth is staring me in the face.
As if to prove the point, Lancer bounds over the wall, fleeing the compound.

page240.text:
"...Hey, Archer. Is that one of your hypotheticals?"
"Perhaps. But now all seven of them are here, Rin."
Archer is calm.
Meanwhile my rational thought goes flying out the window.
What happens next should have been obvious, but I'm not thinking straight.

page241.text:
There's a strong gust of wind.
The clouds cover the sky like an umbrella.
Darkness shrouds the lightless outskirts of the town.
A Servant leaps over the wall and lands gracefully, like an unworldly bird.

page242.text:
"...!"
Archer reacts.
I fail to even twitch in response.
That's my fault.
The fight ends before even a second passes.
One second might be a brief instant to me,
but it's a massive opening to a Servant.

page243.text:
A bladed wind closes in on me.
"Huh? Archer...?"
Archer lunges in front of me,
while the Servant cuts him deeply.
It really was just an instant.
Is Archer, who so gracefully fended off Lancer's brutal assault, going down in one hit...?

page244.text:
"Vanish, Archer!"
I made it in time.
Before the Servant's next strike takes off Archer's head, I force him to retreat.
Pain throbs in my right hand.
Because it was such an extreme order, it used up one of my Command Spells.

page245.text:
...Now I only have one left.
But this was for the best.
It's worth losing a Command Spell or two to make sure Archer doesn't die.

page246.text:
...
Without skipping a beat, the Servant comes for me next.
"...Don't underestimate me!"
I pull out a wind-imbued topaz, and feed magical energy directly into it without any extra steps.

page247.text:
It's a cluster of wind spells that I've been feeding into it day after day, and they're enough to blow away a house or two without leaving a trace.
This is one of ten jewels I've been building up for the last seventeen years, without skipping a single day.
Even if I can't beat this thing with it, it should be enough to slow—
...Or not.
It didn't work at all.
The moment it touches the Servant, what ought to have been a tempest that would hew apart anything in its path disappears like a simple stage magic trick.
What terrifying Magic Resistance.
Are you telling me that a mage doesn't have enough magical energy to hurt this Servant!?

page248.text:
Oh, no.
My magecraft doesn't work, and I've lost Archer's protection. I have no way to stop this Servant.
Even if I barely manage to dodge the first attack, I'm finished.
I look up at the night sky.
In it, I imagine a ruthless reaper coming for me, sprawled pitifully on the ground...

page249.text:
"Wha—"
The wind blows.
Through a break in the clouds, the moon peeks out through the spiral-like sky.
The moonlight highlights her elegant profile.
So this is the face of the Servant who drove off Lancer,
took down my Archer in one blow,
and shrugged off my magecraft like it was nothing.

page250.text: "That was an admirable display of magecraft, mage."

page251.text:
The girl's voice rings clear like a bell.
Yet her voice is the stuff of nightmares at this moment.

page252.text: "But this is the end for you, Master of Archer."

page253.text: The sword she's thrust at me seems to shine.

page254.text:
I know that this is my dying moment.
One glance is enough to figure that out.

page255.text:
This is the card I wished to draw,
the sword-wielding hero said to be the most powerful Servant.

page256.text:
...
I look up at the moon, prepared to die.
There's no room to beg for my life, no time to escape.
With my death, Rin Tohsaka's Holy Grail War will have ended on the third day.
You'd think I'd go out hating my foe, feeling nothing but shame and regret.

page257.text:
...But I don't feel that way at all.
Something's seriously wrong with me.
I'm one moment away from certain death, and here I am, entranced by my killer.
...Yeah.
It's frustrating, to be sure.

page258.text:
But there's nothing I can do now.
...The strongest Servant is going to kill me.
She looks all at once heartless, utterly noble, and so very beautiful...
